sections.heading: Why these two symptoms together matter
paragraphs: Searchers often look up excessive thirst and frequent urination together because the combination can change urgency. Alone, one sign might be “monitor”; together, veterinarians often want a faster call.

Excessive thirst with Frequent urination often needs same-day veterinary guidance, especially if it is new, worsening, or paired with other symptoms. Use the red-flag list to decide whether to call now versus schedule promptly.
Treat overlapping red flags from either symptom as actionable — you do not need both lists to “fully match.”

sections.heading: Causes veterinarians may consider
paragraphs: Possible contributors to excessive thirst: Diabetes mellitus; Kidney disease; Cushing’s disease (more common in dogs).
Possible contributors to frequent urination: Urinary tract infection; Bladder stones; Diabetes.
Overlapping causes (infection, toxins, pain, organ disease) are why combination pages exist — still not a diagnosis.
